newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says worried about drift in Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Italy says worried about drift in Mideast peace.

text.p: Italy said on Thursday it was worried about a stall in the Middle East peace process, saying it had been aggravated by the decision to expand Israeli settlements in occupied territories.
A statement issued after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat held talks with Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini said both expressed concern over a slowing of progress.
Dini and Arafat agreed that the situation could "dangerously worsen because of the lingering absence of progress" in the peace process.
A drift in the peace process had been aggravated "by the recent decision to expand Israeli settlements" in the territories, the statement said.
The two men said a solution to the problem of the town of Hebron in the occupied West Bank would send a powerful signal to put the process back on track.
Hebron is the last of seven West Bank towns from which Israeli troops are supposed to redeploy under previous accords, but the talks are bogged down over security arrangements for Hebron's 400 Jews.
Arafat met Dini as part of a day visit to Rome. He also met Pope John Paul, President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro and Prime Minister Romano Prodi.
